items.title: ttok 1.0
items.summary: Release: ttok 1.0 I released ttok 0.4 , ran uv tool upgrade ttok , piped a file into the new version... and realized that it was defaulting to the GPT-4 tokenizer when it should very clearly default to GPT-5/GPT-6 instead! I figured switching the default was a reasonable excuse to finally ship a 1.0. OpenAI haven't actually confirmed that GPT-6 uses the same tokenizer as the GPT-5 family yet - there's an angry issue about it - but I found this commit by William Liu which reports on an experiment he ran confirming that the tokenizers are likely the same: All seven GPT models (5.5, 5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, 6 Astra/Sol/Luna) report 44,794 tokens and match each other on every one of the 31 fixtures. items.title: Preview: 'Muramasa: Revenant Blades' Polishes Vanillaware's Gem To Shine Brighter Than Ever
items.summary: Reforged. Muramasa: The Demon Blade originally launched on the Wii back in 2009, a title that we called "gorgeous, engrossing, " and even underrated. We’ve been hoping to see a modern port of this gem for a long time now, and Vanillaware has delivered, with Muramasa: Revenant Blades coming to both Switch 1 and 2 in February next year. The PS Vita received Muramasa Rebirth in 2013, bringing updated music and localisation, followed by the Genroku Legends DLC , which added four new playable stories in addition to the original two. Revenant Blades combines Rebirth and Genroku Legends, meaning all six stories are available from launch. Think of this as a 'complete edition', then, finally accessible on current platforms.
